subject: Clarify SOC 2 scope for dedicated pool + VPC peering — evidence request
messages:
From: Natalie Ramos <natalie.ramos@fincore.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-03-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SOC 2 applicability & evidence request for Dedicated + VPC peering

Hi Kimberly,

We’re starting a procurement/security review for Redwood prior to a production rollout and need to confirm scope for SOC 2 Type II coverage. Specifically:

- Our architecture will use a Dedicated GPU pool with VPC peering (private connectivity) for all traffic. We do, however, have a fallback policy in our design that would allow traffic to route to Redwood’s hosted tier if Dedicated capacity is exhausted.

Questions:
1) For a customer using Dedicated + VPC peering, is the Dedicated pool considered "in-scope" for Redwood’s SOC 2 Type II report?
2) Does the hosted fallback path fall within the same SOC 2 period or is that treated as out-of-scope unless traffic actually routes there?
3) Can you provide: the latest SOC 2 Type II report, any bridge letter or attestation that documents coverage for dedicated pools or VPC connector patterns, and a tenant-isolation/tenant-mapping artifact we can reference for PCI/HIPAA impact assessment?

Target period for our audit: Jan 1, 2027 — Dec 31, 2027. If you have an interim bridge letter that maps coverage for fallbacks or mixed routing, that would be helpful.

Please let me know what we can expect to receive and the estimated turnaround. If you’d like, I can share a topology diagram of our environment.

Thanks,
Natalie Ramos
Security Manager, FinCore Bank
security@fincore.com

---

Attachment: fincore_topology_v1.pdf (not attached here; will share on request)

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Natalie Ramos <natalie.ramos@fincore.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-15T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 applicability & evidence request for Dedicated + VPC peering

Hi Natalie — thanks for the clear summary. Looping in Ben (sales lead) so we can coordinate any contractual/rollout language.

Short answers up front:
- Dedicated pools that carry a customer’s production traffic are within the scope of Redwood’s SOC 2 Type II when the pool is part of our managed, auditable infrastructure and customer data is processed on that pool.
- Hosted fallback is treated as a distinct topology for audit purposes: it is not automatically in-scope unless traffic actually routes there during the SOC 2 period. However, we provide a bridge-letter pattern that documents how fallbacks are handled and whether they would be covered depending on the timing.

What we can provide immediately (stubs/initial artifacts):
- SOC2_TypeII_Redwood_2027.pdf (redacted executive summary + report stub)
- bridge_letter_dedicated_to_hosted_2027.txt (explains fallback conditions and how they map to the audit window)
- tenant_isolation_mapping_fincore.csv (high-level tenant mapping for your account — redacted)
- routing_fallback_config_screenshot.png (screenshot of the policy toggle that controls fallback)

Follow-ups / clarifications we need from you:
1) Please confirm whether your deployment will allow automatic fallback (i.e., opt-in on your side) or whether you intend to disable hosted fallback entirely for production.
2) Confirm the exact audit period you want mapped (you mentioned Jan 1–Dec 31, 2027). If you need coverage for any traffic that may have routed to hosted between Mar–Jun 2027, flag that and we’ll prioritize a bridge letter specific to that timeframe.

We can share the redacted SOC 2 PDF and bridge letter within 48 business hours. Tenant mapping and the routing screenshot we can provide as a CSV/PNG the same day. For full unredacted SOC 2 documents we typically require an NDA; the redacted versions work for most security reviews.

Ben — can you and I align on whether procurement needs any additional contractual language for guaranteed no-fallback?

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Security & Compliance (Contracted)
Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai

Signature: kimberly_park — Redwood Inference

---

Attachments to follow: SOC2_TypeII_Redwood_2027.pdf (redacted, stub), bridge_letter_dedicated_to_hosted_2027.txt (stub)

From: Natalie Ramos <natalie.ramos@fincore.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: security@fincore.com
Date: 2028-03-15T12:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 applicability & evidence request for Dedicated + VPC peering

Thanks, Kimberly — helpful summary.

To be explicit: we will be using Dedicated + VPC peering for primary traffic, but we have a documented fallback policy that would allow hosted routing for short periods during large spikes or capacity issues. We prefer the fallback to remain disabled by default, but cannot promise it will never be used during incident scenarios.

We need the following scoped to our audit window (Jan 1–Dec 31, 2027):
- Redacted SOC 2 Type II report for 2027 (preferably within your standard redaction limits).
- A bridge letter that specifically calls out hosted-fallback scenarios and whether such routing during the 2027 window would require separate attestation.
- Tenant mapping that shows our tenant id(s) and whether any routing cross-over occurred during the period. If cross-over occurred, we’ll need timestamps/sample logs.

Can you include a note on sampling methodology (how you choose requests that are included in sample testing) and whether request routing decisions (dedicated -> hosted) are included in SOC 2 control procedures?

Thanks — if it helps, I can send our procurement contact and they can open an NDA quickly for the unredacted materials.

-Natalie

---

Quoted earlier: "For full unredacted SOC 2 documents we typically require an NDA; the redacted versions work for most security reviews."

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Natalie Ramos <natalie.ramos@fincore.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-16T16:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 applicability & evidence request for Dedicated + VPC peering

Hi Natalie — quick update & confirmed deliverables.

1) We will send the redacted SOC2_TypeII_Redwood_2027.pdf and bridge_letter_dedicated_to_hosted_2027.txt by end of day tomorrow (March 17). Those will explicitly map: dedicated-pool coverage, the conditional hosted fallback behavior, and the audit period you specified.

2) Tenant mapping (tenant_isolation_mapping_fincore.csv) — we will provide a redacted mapping file that lists your tenant IDs and a summary column that indicates whether any request routing crossed to hosted during the 2027 window. If we find any cross-over we’ll attach sample routing logs (timestamps + routing decision) as CSV rows.

3) Sampling / control note: requests included in SOC 2 sampling are drawn from production traffic processed by the in-scope infrastructure. Routing decision logic (the code path that evaluates fallback) is included in the control set for the runtime; therefore, if traffic actually executed the hosted fallback during the reporting window, those events are within the audit evidence (and will be noted in our bridge letter). If fallback is merely configured but never used during the period, the hosted environment is not considered in-scope.

Next actions for you: please confirm whether you’re willing to sign a standard NDA for unredacted artifacts (procurement can send it) or if the redacted materials suffice. Also confirm whether you want us to run a targeted query for any cross-over during Mar–Jun 2027 (you mentioned that window earlier). If yes, we’ll prioritize log sampling for that period.

We’ll attach the four artifacts as stubs in the first batch: SOC2_TypeII_Redwood_2027.pdf (redacted stub), bridge_letter_dedicated_to_hosted_2027.txt (stub), tenant_isolation_mapping_fincore.csv (stub), routing_fallback_config_screenshot.png (stub). For any unredacted material we will follow the NDA flow.

Ben — please advise if procurement/legal needs any additional language for a no-fallback guarantee (customer-requested runway).

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Security & Compliance (Contracted)
Redwood Inference
